messages:
Jordan: Pushed a quick perf dashboard showing per-route token latency + GPU telemetry. grafana: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/xyz - take a look when you have a sec
Priya: Nice, thanks. Any signs of regressions after the kernel-selector tweak we deployed yesterday?
Jordan: Quick summary: overall throughput up ~6%, but 95/99 tail on long-prefix chat routes bumped ~10-15ms. I sliced by model and route.
Mateo: Do you have overlap with SM occupancy/VRAM during those windows? Could be a MIG slice imbalance or memory thrash.
Jordan: Yes — here's the PromQL I used to overlay token tail vs SM occupancy:
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))
/
avg_over_time(gpu_sm_occupancy_percent[5m])
```
Priya: Hmm. That division is useful but we should keep them as separate panels too.
Ava: FYI ops noticed VRAM jump ~+120MB on the same timestamps and NV power crept up ~8%. Thermal stayed under 78C but trending.
telemetry-bot: nightly profile uploaded: s3://profiles/runtime/2025-11-02/1807777000.nvprof
Mateo: I inspected nvprof: noticed fallback to `matmul_generic` kernels in a few frames where we expected `matmul_fused_v2`. SM occupancy for those kernels was ~21% vs 45% for fused.
Jordan: I grabbed a small JSON snippet from the trace:
```
{"kernel":"matmul_generic","avg_ms":"0.78","sm_occupancy":"21%","vram_delta_mb":"120"}
{"kernel":"matmul_fused_v2","avg_ms":"0.34","sm_occupancy":"45%","vram_delta_mb":"30"}
```
Priya: That explains the tail. Why did selector pick generic? Inputs with long prefixes + KV cache prefetch might change shapes and push it into a slow path.
Mateo: Also saw extra memcpy calls right before matmul_generic. That smells like KV cache miss/prefetch overhead.
Ava: Can we add a small telemetry label to capture `kvcache.hit` vs `kvcache.miss` per request and export it to the route dashboard? Even a simple counter would help correlate.
Jordan: Plan: add `runtime_kernel.family` label (values: fused, generic, cublas) and `kvcache.hit`/`kvcache.miss` counters. Then create: 1) per-route kernel distribution panel 2) heatmap of SM occupancy per MIG slice 3) VRAM delta overlay on token latency 4) KV hit/miss latency panel.
Priya: For the kernel label keep cardinality low — use family not full function name. We don't want explosion.
Mateo: Also add a small panel: per-model prefix-length vs fused_ratio. That will help identify which prefixes trigger fallback.
Jordan: Agreed. I'll open a PR against telemetry agent and a Grafana dashboard patch.
Ava: Can we also run a canary: `kernel_selector=prefer_fused` for one dedicated pool to validate? If fused ratio improves and tail drops, we can gradually roll it. Need rollback rules if tail regresses.
Mateo: We ran a short canary last week on staging: throughput +5% but 1.8% of heavy routes saw tail regressions because fused misses on edge shapes.
Priya: So add automated rollback: if 99th tail increases >10% and fused_ratio drops >30% relative to baseline in 10m window, revert selector.
Jordan: I'll include those SLOs in the rollout plan. Also adding alert thresholds: GPU slice temperature > 85C, SM occupancy drop > 15% correlated with kernel_family == generic.
telemetry-bot: Created PERF-789: Add kernel labels, KV metrics, and observability dashboards (https://issues.redwood/PERF-789)
Ava: Thanks. Jordan — can you attach the nvprof timeline and a short writeup of suspected cause to PERF-789? :thumbsup:
Jordan: Will do. Uploading the nvprof and a mini writeup now.
Mateo: One extra note — when exporting `runtime_kernel.family` also export a `runtime_kernel.preferred` boolean so we can detect when selector forced fallback vs intentional preference.
Jordan: Good call, adding that.
Priya: Great, once dashboards in place we should run a 24h canary and then iterate on batching heuristics if needed.
Jordan: I'll sync with infra to schedule the canary tomorrow morning (UTC). Thanks everyone. :rocket:
